text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Over 60 percent of the Macedonian citizens have voted at the local elections on Sunday contested by 33 political parties, nine coalitions and the same number of independent candidates. The elections passed without serious incidents, although many complaints were filed to the state election commission. International observers have still not given their report.

- Unofficially most of the votes are divided between the ruling SDAM and the opposition coalition VRMO-DPMNE, the Democratic party and the MAAK conservative party. Strong competition in western Macedonia between the ethnic Albanian PDP and PDPA parties.
- In Skopje SDAM candidate Jovica Ugrinovski and opposition candidate Risto Penov (coalition VMRO-DPMNE-DP and MAAK conservative party) and the independent candidate Ljupco Nikolovski are very close.
- Independent candidate for Skopje mayor Velibor Djarovski complained because his name was not registered in election lists and he was not able to vote.
- Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov said that "after this election Macedonia has all elements of a modern democratic state."
